text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it does not plan to put new commercial banks under a special supervision, rejecting allegations in local media. The BNB has put on September 23 nine banks under a special supervision due to a danger of insolvency.

-- Bulgaria's trade unions should organise strikes rather then rallies if they want to put forward their demands to the Socialists' cabinet, the leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces Ivan Kostov said.
Kostov referred to a protest rally against the economic policy of the ruling Socialists held on Tueaday in Sofia.
-- Some seven tonnes of cannabis were seized by police in villages near the south-western towns of Petrich and Sandanski, the interior ministry said.
-- The BNB board is expected to discuss today the offer by the state-owned Bulbank to buy a majority stake in the state Economic Bank, which was placed under a special supervision on September 23.
-- Electricity and central heating prices are expected to rise by 15 percent from November 1 due to a 18,8 percent monthly inflation in September, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Russia's prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin declined a meeting with Bulgaria's culture minister and Socialist Party presidential candidate Ivan Marazov, because of a busy schedule, the newspaper said.
-- Bulgaria's deputy transport minister Vassil Rangelov and his Macedonian counterpart Branko Petrovsky agreed in Skopje to lift all road tolls between the two countries from next year.

-- Senior officials from the nine banks placed under special supervision by the BNB in September are under constant surveilance, as they are suspected of threatening Bulgaria's national security, National Security Service official said.
-- Bulgaria's finance ministry said it would start to issue inflation-linked government securities from next year.

-- Bulgaria's current record-high main interest rate of 300 percent, in force from September 24, will be able to contain the dollar's rise on the local forex market only for a month or two, deputy economic minister Gancho Ganchev said.
-- Bulgaria and Russia have agreed to set up joint ventures in military industry, said Bulgaria's interior minister Nikolai Dobrev, winding up a visit to Moscow. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
